📖 Core Definitions

Essential Terminology & Concepts

Data Visualisation And Python Key Concept

As discussed in previous units, data wrangling is used to prepare data for analysis.

Figures And Subplots Key Concept

In a single canvas, you can create several sub-plots.

Annotations Key Concept

Annotations can be used to highlight some of the key points of a graph.

📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

6.2 Data Visualisation and Python

  • As discussed in previous units, data wrangling is used to prepare data for analysis.
  • However, before you start analysing data, you may like to represent the data in a graphical form that is easy to interpret.
  • Visualisation helps to communicate information to the users more effectively, provided the correct form of visualisation is used.
  • The matplotlib library in Python, an open-source library, allows you to create various types of plots, including line graphs, pie charts, scatter plots, and more.

6.2.1 Figures and Subplots

  • In a single canvas, you can create several sub-plots.
  • We demonstrate this with the help of an example.
  • ii) A bar chart of Department and Total Salary iii) A pie chart on Specialisation and Total Salary and iv) A line chart on Department and Average of YearsWorking.
  • subplot [1, 0].pie(slicesofsumsalary , labels = labelslist, ) subplot [1, 0].set_title("Pie Chart of Total Salary for Different Specialisations") # Part (e): Bottom-Right: A line chart on Department and Average of YearsWorking.

6.3 Customisation of Chart Elements and Layout

  • Data visualisation is an art of representing data in a form that can help interpret the basic characteristics of data.
  • Therefore, a graph should have proper layout, labels, colour, etc.
  • This section explains how the matplotlib library can be used to add different features to a graph.
  • Colours, Markers, Line Styles, Ticks and Legends Colours are useful in highlighting information in a graph where you want to draw the attention of a person.

6.3.1 Colours, Markers, Line Styles, Ticks and Legends

  • Colours are useful in highlighting information in a graph where you want to draw the attention of a person.
  • Markers, on the other hand, point to an exact location in a graph.
  • And line styles can be used to distinguish the importance of different types of lines in a graph.
  • Ticks are useful guides if your scale of display is very large.

6.3.2 Annotations

  • Annotations can be used to highlight some of the key points of a graph.
  • The main purpose is to draw attention to certain important aspects of the graphs.
  • Annotations help in increasing the clarity of information being represented by graphs.
  • There are several ways of annotating a graph, such as you can add an arrow or a label, etc.

6.4 Saving Plots to a File

  • They are drawn to represent certain characteristics of data so that users and decision makers can interpret them easily.
  • Therefore, plots are to be shared with decision makers and other stakeholders.
  • This requires graphs to be saved in a format such that they can be included in different reports.
  • Part (a) creates the dataframe named Employee_data 2.

6.5 Use of Configuration in Matplotlib

  • You can set different parameters in this file using this dictionary.
  • plt.rcParams['axes.labelsize'] = 14 Alternatively, you can use a function plt.rc() to change parameters.
  • For example, one of the popular style is ggplot.
  • A detailed discussion on this topic is beyond the scope of this unit.

6.6 Plotting with pandas and seaborn

  • In addition to matplotlib library, you can plot with pandas and seaborn libraries.
  • The following are some of the functions that you can use to make plots.
  • The pandas library has a plot() function that can be used to plot a graph and seaborn library can be used for advanced statistical plots.
  • Part (a) creates the dataframe named Employee_data.
